QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_18

question.text: Per the current NISM VIII workbook (pp.162–163), how is the exposure/extreme-loss margin for derivatives positions determined?

answer.text: A fixed 3% of the notional value of the contract for index futures
A fixed 5% of the notional value of the contract for all derivatives
Capital Market segment VaR and Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) percentages are applied on client-level settlement obligations

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM VIII workbook (pp.162–163) describes the margin framework in terms of Capital Market VaR and Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) percentages applied on client-level settlement obligations. The earlier fixed-percentage exposure-margin rules (e.g., 3% for index futures) are not supported by the December 2025 workbook pages checked. The Trap: The legacy 3% and 5% fixed-percentage framings are the trap; the current workbook uses risk-based VaR + ELM percentages. Cross-Exam Context: NISM VIII and VII both test the current VaR/ELM margin framework over the legacy fixed-percentage formulation.
